finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated 'q' query parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL LIKE clause, allowing UNION-based reads of any table in shop.db (including schema via sqlite_master).
finding.source: app.py:11 — request.args.get('q', '') supplied by any remote, unauthenticated client.
finding.sink: app.py:12 — db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'"), results returned as JSON at app.py:13.

trace.note: /search route registered with no authentication or authorization
q read from request query string with no validation
q concatenated into SQL text via f-string; no parameter binding
all result rows returned to the attacker as JSON

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no input validation, escaping, allowlist, parameter binding, or length limit. sqlite3 rejects stacked statements, so the attack is limited to single-SELECT reads (UNION), which is still sufficient for full read exfiltration. Schema of shop.db not in repo, so exact exploitable tables are unknown.

verdict.reason: app.py:9 registers /search with no auth, app.py:11 takes q directly from request.args, app.py:12 interpolates it into an f-string passed to db.execute with no parameter binding, and app.py:13 returns all rows as JSON, so an anonymous attacker can run UNION-based reads.

finding.claim: Possible missing authorization in /by-owner: any unauthenticated caller can list product id/name for any owner by supplying the owner value, with no check that the caller is that owner or is entitled to see the listing. Lower confidence; depends on whether ownership-to-product mapping is meant to be private.
finding.source: app.py:24 — request.args.get('owner', '') supplied by any remote, unauthenticated client.
finding.sink: app.py:25-26 — parameterized SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE owner = ?, returned as JSON.

trace.note: /by-owner route registered with no authentication or authorization
owner taken from query string, attacker-chosen
parameterized query filters products by attacker-supplied owner (no SQL injection)
matching id and name rows returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Query is parameterized (no SQLi). No ownership or session check exists anywhere in the app. Whether this is intended public behavior cannot be determined from the repo alone.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:22 registers /by-owner with no auth decorator or session check, app.py:24 reads owner from request.args, and app.py:25-26 runs a parameterized SELECT and returns id and name. The only protection is the parameterized query, which blocks SQL injection but not unauthorized access.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate and an anonymous caller can list any owner's product ids and names via app.py:22-26 with no control in between. Whether that is a defect depends on whether owner-to-product mapping is meant to be private, and the app is a public catalog (/search at app.py:9-13 and /product at app.py:16-19 are also unauthenticated), so the repo alone cannot settle it.
